children: Hungary's government expects the budget deficit to fall to 2.8% of economic output by 2030, below the European Union's 3% ceiling, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Tuesday.
"The Finance Ministry's forecast puts (the deficit) at 4% in 2028, 3.4% in 2029 and below 3%, at 2.8% in 2030," Magyar told public radio in an interview.
Economic growth could accelerate to more than 3% by the end of the government's term in 2030 and was expected to reach 2.4% in 2027, he said.
Public debt is expected to decline to 77.2% of GDP next year, he added.

Magyar said public sector wage increases, tax cuts and pension hikes would boost households' disposable income and support consumption, although stronger consumption would also have a slightly inflationary effect.
Hungary could not currently specify a target date for adopting the euro, he said.
He added that current inflation was "extremely low" and forecast inflation at 3% next year, saying this would still represent a healthy rate of price growth.
